title: CIA Director Ratcliffe Makes Unannounced Trip to Moscow
dek: CIA Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Moscow on August 25, 2026, in an unannounced visit confirmed by flight tracking and multiple outlets. Neither Washington nor Moscow disclosed the purpose or who he met. Ukraine paused drone strikes during his presence and resumed attacks hours after his departure.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: A C-17 transport plane carrying CIA Director Ratcliffe departed Latvia, landed at Moscow's Vnukovo airport at approximately 07:04 GMT, and returned to Latvia before 17:00 GMT on August 25, per BBC reporting of FlightRadar24 data.
bottom_line: The actual substance and outcome of Ratcliffe's Moscow visit remain undisclosed. Watch for any official statements from the US or Russian governments, and any subsequent developments in prisoner releases, escalation dynamics, or Ukraine negotiations that might clarify the trip's purpose.
body: CIA Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Moscow on August 25, 2026, for unannounced talks, according to reporting by BBC News citing CBS and flight tracking data. A C-17 military transport plane departed Riga airport at 05:50 GMT, landed at Moscow's Vnukovo airport at approximately 07:04 GMT, and returned to Riga before 17:00 GMT the same day, per FlightRadar24 data reported by BBC News.
Neither Washington nor Moscow has disclosed the purpose of the visit or who Ratcliffe met during his time on the ground.

Prior to the trip, the US informed Ukraine that a senior delegation would travel to Moscow and asked Kyiv to suspend strikes until they departed, according to BBC reporting of CBS sourcing. Ukraine agreed to pause drone and missile attacks against Moscow during Ratcliffe's presence, per ABC News reporting. Ukraine resumed drone attacks on Moscow overnight into Wednesday morning, hours after the plane carrying Ratcliffe left Russia, ABC News reports. Moscow's Mayor Sergey Sobyanin stated that at least 10 drones were shot down while flying toward the capital, and Russia's federal air transport agency reported temporary flight restrictions at three of Moscow's four international airports.

Footage posted on social media showed the C-17 approaching Vnukovo airport and a diplomatic motorcade traveling through Moscow, per BBC reporting. BBC News reports this trip is thought to be Ratcliffe's first visit to Russia as CIA director, although he has maintained contact with his intelligence counterparts there.

According to BBC News, experts and former officials have suggested possible purposes for the visit. John Foreman, who served as a British military attaché to Moscow between 2019 and 2022, told BBC News the visit could focus on escalation management given speculation that recent drone activity in Germany could be linked to Russia. Foreman also told BBC that the trip could concern the release of US detainees held in Russia. BBC News reports that Ratcliffe played a role in negotiations for the release of Russian-American citizen Ksenia Karelina, who was jailed in Russia for over a year after being accused of providing support to Ukraine. The CIA was involved in a 2024 prisoner swap deal with Russia that resulted in the release of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich, former US Marine Paul Whelan, and Russian-American journalist Alsu Kurmasheva, per BBC reporting.

BBC News notes that in-person talks between high-level American and Russian officials are rare. Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin at a summit in Alaska last year, but that meeting did not lead to a breakthrough, BBC reports. Subsequent US-led peace talks between Russia and Ukraine appear to have stalled, according to BBC News.
